body.objective: Students will be able to refine technical passages.
successCriteria: I can identify the hardest passages in a piece
I can use slow practice, chunking and rhythm variations to master them
I can measure my progress with a metronome log
body.hook: Professional musicians often practise a hard passage at half speed, perfectly, many times, before playing it at tempo. It seems slow, but it's the fastest way to get it right. In Instrumental Music 30, you'll learn to practise like a professional.

study.title: Practise Like a Pro
study.question: How do professionals master difficult passages?
study.passage:
Step 1, Find the problem (5 minutes): Play through your concert piece and mark the two hardest passages with brackets.
Step 2, Diagnose (5 minutes): Is the problem notes, rhythm, fingering, tonguing, breathing or endurance? Write it down.
Step 3, Chunk (10 minutes): Break the passage into chunks of one or two beats. Practise each chunk, then link chunk 1 to the first note of chunk 2 ("chaining").
Step 4, Slow practice (10 minutes): Set the metronome at half the target tempo. Play the passage 3 times in a row perfectly before moving the metronome up by 4–8 beats per minute. A mistake means going back down.
Step 5, Rhythm variations (5 minutes): Play the passage long-short, then short-long, then in triplets. This strengthens weak finger or stick combinations.
Step 6, Context (5 minutes): Play from four bars before the passage to four bars after, so it connects musically.
Practice log: date, passage, starting tempo, ending tempo, what improved.
Professional habit: Stop practising a passage while it's still going well, rather than when you're tired and making mistakes.
